title: Rumen-reticulum junction, Rumination, and Four stomach compartments
text:
3. Rumen-reticulum junction
○ Main function is to prevent large feed particles to pass through the 3rd chamber.
○ Helps in pushing the food back to the esophagus for rumination.
○ Reticulum traps foreign objects such as nails and other hardware.

4. Rumination
○ Once the cow is done eating, it lies down and begins to ruminate.
○ Rumination or cud-chewing is the process by which the cow regurgitates previously consumed feed and chews further.
○ Regurgitation - is a normal physiological process for cows for digesting food.
○ Cud - partly digested food returned from the first stomach of ruminants to the mouth for further chewing.

facts: The main function of the rumen-reticulum junction is to prevent large feed particles from passing through to the 3rd chamber.
The rumen-reticulum junction helps in pushing food back to the esophagus for rumination.
The reticulum traps foreign objects such as nails and other hardware.
Once a cow is done eating, it lies down and begins to ruminate.
Rumination or cud-chewing is the process by which a cow regurgitates previously consumed feed and chews it further.
Regurgitation is a normal physiological process for cows for digesting food.
Cud is defined as partly digested food returned from the first stomach of ruminants to the mouth for further chewing.
The four stomach compartments of a cow are the Rumen, Reticulum, Omasum, and Abomasum.
